physicalNotes: Radius 0.23258136 Jupiter radii from Garai et al. 2023 (2023A&A...674A..44G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...674A..44G/abstract): 16,627.7 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. No mass is measured: Garai et al. 2023 (2023A&A...674A..44G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...674A..44G/abstract) gives only an upper limit of 0.08359857 Jupiter masses, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Garai et al. 2023 (2023A&A...674A..44G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname GARAI_ET_AL__2023): P 47.42489 d
sources.shape: Garai et al. 2023 (2023A&A...674A..44G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname GARAI_ET_AL__2023): a/R* 57; Garai et al. 2023 (2023A&A...674A..44G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname GARAI_ET_AL__2023): inclination derived from its impact parameter 0.456 with its a/R* 57 (Winn 2010, eq. 7)
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Garai et al. 2023 (2023A&A...674A..44G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname GARAI_ET_AL__2023): transit mid-time 2459136.5372 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 6 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
